🤷 Two crowds. One establishment. One weekend. Two completely opposite verdicts.

👉 Notting Hill Carnival: 7,000+ police, 169 arrests on the FIRST DAY (243 with the approach roads) — weapons, drugs, sexual offences, assaults on emergency workers, and two knife attacks.
The verdict? "Mood overwhelmingly positive." A peaceful celebration.

👉 Portsmouth: ~140 men landed in a single dinghy at Eastney — just 3-4 miles from HMNB Portsmouth, the home of the Royal Navy and HMS Prince of Wales. Unidentified, unvetted, undetected until they were almost on the sand. Ordinary residents came out in protest.
The verdict? "Intimidating and thuggish." They "crossed the line."

Put them side by side — because they're banking on you not doing it.

Actual stabbings, sexual offences and assaults on police = "overwhelmingly positive."
Taxpayers angry their border has failed = "thuggish."

You can't explain that by conduct — the conduct runs the OTHER way. You can only explain it by politics: which crowd the people in charge approve of.

To be fair: most at Carnival are law-abiding, and genuine violence at any protest is wrong. But apply it evenly. If a few bad actors don't define the Carnival, they don't define Portsmouth either.

Reform UK: one standard, for everyone. Defending your borders is not thuggery — and calling knife crime a triumph doesn't make anyone safer.
